panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 9 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I). A: X-ray of the left hip showing shepherd's crook deformity and fracture of the proximal femur, consistent with osteofibrous dysplasia. B: X-ray of the lower leg showing a pathologic fracture of the tibia, a manifestation of osteofibrous dysplasia. C: X-ray of the lower leg showing tibial fracture managed with external fixation, indicating osteofibrous dysplasia. D: CT scan of the chest showing a lesion in the rib, consistent with polyostotic osteofibrous dysplasia. E: Lung window CT of the chest, part of the preoperative imaging showing thoracic involvement. F: CT scan of the hip showing a lesion in the acetabulum, consistent with osteofibrous dysplasia. G: Axial CT of the pelvis showing bone lesions in the pelvic bones. H: CT scan showing the pelvic bones and proximal femur with lesions consistent with osteofibrous dysplasia. I: X-ray of the left hip demonstrating deformity consistent with osteofibrous dysplasia.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies multiple intracortical lesions centered in the distal tibial cortex, with additional posteromedial fibular cortical lesions.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: T1-weighted MRI shows multiple cortical lesions of the distal right tibia and fibula with the characteristic intracortical distribution of osteofibrous dysplasia. Arrows annotate the lesions. B: T2 DIXON WATER MRI demonstrates the multifocal intracortical tibial and fibular lesions described in the caption. Arrows mark the involved cortical regions. C: Post-gadolinium MRI shows enhancing intracortical lesions in the distal tibia and fibula, consistent with the captioned osteofibrous dysplasia findings. Arrows annotate the lesions.
panels.attribution_text: Chabot and Janssens. Osteofibrous Dysplasia Involving Both Tibia and Fibula: A Rare Campanacci‑Type Presentation.. Journal of the Belgian Society of Radiology 2025. doi:10.5334/jbsr.4060. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: MRI of the distal right leg: T1‑weighted (A), T2 DIXON WATER (B), and post‑gadolinium contrast‑enhanced (C) sequences. Multiple intracortical lesions are centered in the cortex of the distal tibia, primarily involving the posterolateral and anterolateral aspects, with some extension into the anterior cortex (arrows). The lesions are hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2 DIXON WATER, and show homogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration. Additional small lesions are noted in the posteromedial cortex of the fibula.
in_text_mentions: ibia, predominantly involving the posterolateral and anterolateral aspects, with some extension into the anterior cortex. These lesions showed low signal intensity on T1‑weighted images, high signal on T2 DIXON WATER sequences, and homogeneous, diffuse enhancement after gadolinium administration. Millimetric lesions were also observed in the posteromedial cortex of the fibula (Figure 3, arrows). Overall, the imaging features suggested an intracortical lesion of subperiosteal origin that was largely contained within the bone contours and did not extend into the medullary cavity or soft tissues.
